title: Backfill historical SLO/error budget calculations (Q4/Q1) to validate targets + calibrate burn alerts
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Context
We need an objective backtest of the proposed tiered SLO targets (Hosted vs Dedicated) and the burn-rate alert thresholds before we finalize policy + switch gates beyond warn-only. We’ve had multiple recent issues where SLI correctness (timeouts/499/streaming disconnect attribution) materially changes burn-rate behavior; this ticket makes that visible with historical replay.

Goal
Compute historical SLIs/SLO attainment + error budget burn for Q4 and Q1-to-date, and use the results to:
1) Validate the proposed targets in the Tiered SLO definitions doc (are we setting targets above current reality / below customer expectations?)
2) Calibrate burn-rate alert thresholds to reduce noise while still catching real incidents
3) Identify SLI definition gaps (esp. streaming disconnect classification and timeout attribution) before enforcement becomes blocking

Time range (initial)
- Q4 2025: 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31
- Q1 2026 (partial): 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-15
If the pipeline is stable, extend through “now” and keep it running weekly until Phase 2 enforcement is fully rolled out.

Scope
- Hosted tier backfill (global, multi-tenant):
  - /v1/chat/completions (streaming + non-streaming)
  - /v1/completions (where still used)
  - /v1/embeddings
  - Key SLIs: success/availability (5xx + server-side timeouts), streaming disconnect rate (server fault only), p95/p99 latency, streaming TTFT (p95)
- Dedicated tier backfill (customer-scoped without leaking customer identifiers outside restricted views):
  - Availability + latency for dedicated routes
  - Pool readiness SLI (where signals exist in historical data)

Key requirements / constraints
- Tier attribution in historical data:
  - Post-tier-propagation metrics are only available after the tier label was added (gateway → routing → runtime). For earlier periods, backfill must infer tier from request metadata (tenant type / dedicated pool id / auth plan), with explicit “unknown_tier” bucket when inference is ambiguous.
- Cardinality budget:
  - Backfill outputs must use the same aggregation rules as prod dashboards/alerts: tier, region, route_group, service, model_family (no per-model-per-route explosion).
- Data correctness:
  - Avoid counting customer-side cancellations as server failures (e.g., 499) unless SLI spec says otherwise.
  - Streaming disconnects must follow the agreed taxonomy (client abort vs server disconnect).

Proposed implementation
1) Implement a backfill job (batch) that:
   - Reads request-level metrics/log-derived counters from the metrics store for the defined time range
   - Applies canonical SLI definitions (same library as the online budget computation)
   - Computes rolling-window SLO compliance + error budget remaining (e.g., 28d rolling) and burn-rate signals (5m/1h, 30m/6h, 2h/1d) consistent with alerting standard
   - Writes results to a durable table (e.g., slo_budget_history) keyed by: {tier, region, route_group, service, slo_name, window}
2) Produce a summary report for SRE + PMs:
   - “Would this page?” analysis using current proposed burn thresholds
   - Top drivers of burn by week (timeouts vs 5xx vs disconnect vs latency)
   - Dedicated readiness: how often did we dip below readiness targets and for how long (to set initial paging vs ticket-only posture)
3) Validate against known incident timelines and existing dashboards:
   - Spot-check at least 3 incidents in Q4/Q1 and ensure burn spikes align with incident start/end
   - Compare aggregate availability vs the existing legacy availability dashboard and reconcile deltas (document exclusions)

Deliverables
- Backfill job merged and runnable on demand (and optionally scheduled weekly until we stabilize)
- Backfilled dataset for Q4 + Q1-to-date in the metrics warehouse (restricted for Dedicated slices)
- Written summary in ticket comments with:
  - Recommended adjustments (if any) to SLO targets
  - Recommended adjustments (if any) to burn-rate alert thresholds per tier
  - Data quality gaps and follow-up tickets

Acceptance criteria
- Can run backfill end-to-end in < 2 hours for the full time range with bounded query cost
- Aggregate Hosted availability numbers match within ±0.1% vs validated log-based counts for a sampled week (documented sampling method)
- For streaming endpoints, TTFT and disconnect burn behave sensibly: no “always burning” baseline attributable to client aborts
- Output is usable to answer: “If we had gates enabled, would they have blocked releases during <incident X> week?”

Owners / reviewers
- DRI: Nadia Rahman
- SRE review: Aisha Bello, Rafael Mendes
- Gateway/streaming attribution consult: Amara Diallo
- Cardinality/labeling consult: Thomas Baird

Notes
This ticket is intentionally not trying to backfill per-model targets; we need tier/route_group correctness first. Model-level analysis can be a follow-up once we trust the tier + disconnect classification.
activity: 2026-01-21 (Nadia Rahman): Started with a dry-run for Hosted /v1/embeddings using existing recording rules. Preliminary result: availability burn is dominated by a small number of timeout spikes; need to ensure we’re not counting client-side deadline exceeded as server timeout.

2026-01-29 (Aisha Bello): Please treat 499 as client cancel by default (exclude from server-fault availability SLI) unless we have strong evidence it’s server-initiated disconnect. This was a major source of false burn in earlier validation.

2026-02-04 (Thomas Baird): Confirmed aggregation plan: route_group + model_family only. Do not include raw model id in backfill storage keys. If we need per-model drilldowns, store them in an offline extract, not in the primary table.

2026-02-11 (Nadia Rahman): First full Q4 backfill attempt ran into retention gaps for some high-cardinality labels (expected). Adjusted to consume the same low-cardinality aggregates as dashboards. Remaining issue: tier inference for pre-propagation period needs explicit ‘unknown_tier’ handling.

2026-02-16 (Amara Diallo): Streaming disconnect attribution changed after gateway instrumentation update; backfill must use the pre-change mapping for Q4 or we’ll misclassify disconnects. Suggest: version the mapping by date boundary and document it in the report.

2026-02-23 (Nadia Rahman): Implemented v0 of the backfill pipeline and produced a Q1-to-date sample for Hosted chat streaming. Result: proposed fast-burn paging threshold would have paged ~2.3x/day during one noisy week; likely needs anti-flap/tuning or improved disconnect classification. Next: rerun after ENG-2428 instrumentation alignment and recalc.
